external_entities.name: shoppers
external_entities.description: People who browse the storefront, sign in, and place orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that shoppers use to browse and place orders and that receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: Shoppers authenticate with email and password and receive a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The worker uses a database password supplied through an environment variable.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.authentication: email and password; session cookie; MFA none

data_flows.name: call order service
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the third-party card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is confidential because it stores receipts for completed orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order produces a receipt stored in the receipt archive.
